dedupe_keys.name: itu r reference antenna patterns for earth station and space station antennas

description: This ITU-R software page lists the standard antenna radiation patterns used in satellite network filing and coordination, grouped into earth station antenna patterns and space station antenna patterns, plus guidance on submitting antenna radiation patterns. Each earth station entry gives a pattern name, an identifier such as APERR_001V01, a description and receiving and transmitting pattern ids; examples are the Appendix 8 pattern for geostationary networks with gain above 9.3 dB, the Appendix 30 and 30A broadcasting-satellite reference patterns for Regions 1, 2 and 3, the Appendix 7 pattern for coordination areas between 100 MHz and 105 GHz, and Recommendations ITU-R S.465, S.580, S.1855, M.694 and BO.1900. Producer: the ITU Radiocommunication Bureau, which manages satellite frequency filings. Coverage: reference patterns applicable worldwide. Access: a public web page in the ITU-R software section; the page itself lists identifiers and descriptions, and pattern files are handled through ITU software. Licence and cost: no licence stated; the page is free to read. Caveats: these are reference (standard) patterns for coordination and interference assessment, not measured patterns of a specific antenna. Simulation uses: they parameterise interference and link-budget calculations in satellite and terrestrial capacity-planning models. Related record: the ITU-R Study Group 3 propagation databanks (data-itu-r-dbsg3-propagation-databanks).
